subject: Trading
title: Indices and Benchmarks
description: A short lesson to help you apply Indices and Benchmarks.

hook.text: The S&P 500 isn't a stock you can buy. It's a number that tracks 500 companies—a market thermometer.

buildup.text: Indices like the S&P, Dow, and Nasdaq aggregate hundreds of stocks into a single performance metric.

discovery.text: They're market-cap weighted: Apple matters more than a small company because it's worth more.

twist.text: A rising index can hide trouble. If five mega-cap stocks rise while 495 others fall, the index still goes up.

climax.text: Indices set benchmarks. Most active fund managers fail to beat them over time—a humbling fact.

punchline.text: The index is the scoreboard, not the game.

quiz.question: What does 'market-cap weighted' mean for an index?
options: Larger companies have more influence on the index
